2. After withdrawing the execution case the appellant filed Miscellaneous case No. 884 of 1979 for review of tree decree. On 4th July; 1981, the date fixed for per-emptory hearing appellant's Advocate could not attend the Court due to illness. The review application was dismissed for default. 

 3. On 13th January, 1982 the appellant filed an application under Order 47, rule 7(2) of the Civil Procedure Code read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the case after vacating the order of dismissal. The learned Subordinate judge held that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing before the Court on the date of hearing for review application. He, however, dismissed the application for restoration as it was filed long after the expiry of 15 days, prescribed in Article 160 of the Limitation Act. 

 4. The appellant contends that the provisions of Order XLVII, rule 7(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure are attracted in this case, and that as the appellant was prevented by sulfide eat cause from appearing on the date or hear, lug of the review application the court ought to have restored the Miscellaneous case after applying the principles section 5 of the Limitation Act. In support of this contention reliance is placed on Md. Chand Miah Sowdagar Vs, SMH Rahman 1985 RLD 337, and Kalu vs, Sowaria 27 IC 703. The first case has no relevance. The Court's power to admit an appeal under section 5 of the Limitation  Act rafter the expiry of a period, prescribed by a special law came up for decision In that case. The decision reported in 27 1.C. 703 is worth quoting for its admirable brevity: 

 5. The learned Counsel for The appellant has laid much stress on the words in parenthesis, marked by learned Judge himself, in the above decision, and submitted that as in the present case when sufficient cause was found to the satisfaction of the Court for non-appearance of the appellant the petition of review ought to have been restored. Section 5 of the Limitation Act provides for extension of time for an application of review but not for the restoration of application for review rejected for the applicant's failure to appear on the date of hearing, Provision for restoration of a review application, contained in sub-rule (2) of rule 7 of Order 47 of the Code, it subject to Article 160 of the Limitation Act. The applicant is to satisfy the Court within time fixed wider Article 160 of the Limitation Act, that he was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing on the date fixed. The Court has got no power to extend the period prescribed for filing an application for restoration. The reason is not far to seek. Review is an extra-ordinary remedy. He who seeks review of a Court’s order must be vigilant. If his application for review is dismissed for his non-appearance he would rush to the Court, law says within fifteen days, for its restoration.
